title: The 20-Year Hunt for the Impossible Jump in Ocean Temple
creator: Bashir Ko
description:
In 2006 someone posted a blurry clip of a jump that shouldn't be possible. It took the community twenty years to figure out how.

Runs shown in this video belong to their runners, links in the pinned comment.

Discord: https://discord.gg/frameperfect

sentences.t: In two thousand six, somebody uploaded a forty second clip to a tiny forum for a game almost nobody remembers.
The game is called Ocean Temple, a little platformer from a studio that went bust a year after it came out.
And in that clip, the player does a jump in the third level that skips nearly half of the game.
The problem is, nobody could ever do it again.
The person who posted it vanished, the account was deleted, and the clip was about the resolution of a postage stamp.
For twenty years, the speedrunning community argued about whether it was even real.
Today I want to walk you through how they finally cracked it.
So the jump happens at a spot everyone calls the Pillar.
Normally you climb a long staircase of moving platforms to get over a wall.
In the clip, the player just runs at the wall, does something we can't quite see, and launches clean over the top.
For years people tried everything, frame perfect jumps, wall clips, damage boosts off the crabs.
Nothing worked, and a lot of people decided the clip was edited.
Then in twenty nineteen, a runner called Tidewell started taking the game's code apart.
Have you ever been one input away from a world record and had your controller just decide to drift?
That's exactly what Gripline controllers are built to stop, and they're sponsoring today's video.
They use magnetic sticks that don't wear out, so no drift, and the triggers and buttons are swappable if you want shorter travel.
Use code FRAME10 at gripline.gg for ten percent off.
So, Tidewell found something really strange in the physics code.
When your character lands on a moving platform, the game adds the platform's speed to yours for exactly one frame.
And if you jump on that exact frame, you keep the extra speed in the air.
On its own that's a small boost, it's not enough to clear the Pillar.
But Tidewell noticed something else.
If you pause the game on that same frame, the boost gets applied twice.
So the trick wasn't one impossible input, it was a jump and a pause on the same sixtieth of a second, with the stick held just right.
And suddenly the blurry clip made sense, because if you look closely, there's a tiny flicker right before the jump.
That flicker is the pause menu.
For almost twenty years, people thought it was compression artifacts.
Of course, knowing how it works and actually doing it are two very different things.
The window is a single frame, and on original hardware, the input lag makes it even worse.
It took another year before anyone landed it in a real run.
That was a runner named Marisol, on stream, at about three in the morning, and you can hear her chat absolutely losing it.
The world record dropped from forty one minutes to twenty three overnight.
And the craziest part of the whole story came a few months later.
The person who posted the original clip finally came forward on the Discord.
They were twelve when they recorded it, they'd found it completely by accident, and they couldn't do it again either.
They'd deleted the account because people kept calling them a liar.
So the impossible jump was real all along, discovered by a kid who pressed pause at the wrong moment.
I love this community so much.
If you know another legendary trick like this, put it in the comments, because I want to cover more of these.
See you next time.
